newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off, hit by brokerage woes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off, hit by brokerage woes.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier on Wednesday as worries about Japan's widening brokerage scandals and weak June industrial output data weighed on the market, dealers said.
Dealers said news of a raid at the offices of Yamaichi Securities and of the brokerage's involvement with racketeers kept Nikkei cash and futures markets under pressure.
Nikkei 225 September futures ended 185 points lower at 20,220 after hitting an early high of 20,440.
Dealers said the market should be well supported at the psychological 20,000 level but a breach of the 20,600 barrier was looking increasingly remote.
"Given the scenario of the Japanese economy having a relapse, the Nikkei will remain under pressure," a dealer at a European futures house said.
Sentiment would be badly damaged if the market fell through the 20,000 level, he added.
On Taiwan futures, the August MSCI contract added 0.5 to settle at 426.9 on volume of 1,981 lots.
